reports.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
reports.description: Official consumer price index measuring changes in the prices of a basket of goods and services. Released on a regular cadence and used as the primary domestic inflation measure.

reports.title: National Accounts (GDP)
reports.description: Official national accounts estimates of gross domestic product and related aggregates, covering both oil and non-oil activity.

reports.title: Monthly Statistical Bulletin — Banking & Monetary Statistics
reports.description: Monthly compilation of monetary aggregates (M1, M2, M3), central-bank assets and liabilities, gross international reserves, bank deposits, credit and related banking indicators.

reports.title: Population estimates
reports.description: Official population estimates for the UAE, reflecting the large non-national component of the resident population. Most recently reported at approximately 11.3 million (2024) — earlier batch drafts using a ~10 million figure are stale.

reports.title: Balance of Payments
reports.description: Official balance-of-payments statistics compiled according to BPM6, covering the current, capital and financial accounts.

reports.title: Education statistics (general and higher education)
reports.description: Official statistics on general education and higher education enrolment and related indicators.

reports.title: Health services statistics
reports.description: Official statistics on health services.

reports.title: CBUAE Base Rate decisions (Overnight Deposit Facility)
reports.description: Policy interest-rate decisions for the Base Rate applicable to the Overnight Deposit Facility. The rate is anchored to the US Federal Reserve's Interest Rate on Reserve Balances (IORB) and signals the monetary-policy stance under the dirham peg. VERIFIED: multiple 2026 reports confirm CBUAE explicitly holds/moves the Base Rate 'following Fed decision.'

reports.title: Dubai overnight visitor arrivals and tourism performance
reports.publisher: Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism
reports.description: Official statistics on overnight visitor arrivals to Dubai and related tourism performance indicators (occupancy, source markets). Dubai is the dominant tourism destination within the UAE.

reports.title: UAE–GCC merchandise trade statistics
reports.description: Statistics on merchandise trade between the UAE and other GCC member states. Total trade volume reached AED 333 billion in 2024 (imports AED 84.5bn, non-oil exports AED 85.6bn, re-exports AED 162.9bn) — VERIFIED verbatim against the MOF's own page. Reflects the UAE's position inside the GCC Customs Union and Common Market.

reports.title: Banking sector total assets, deposits and gross credit
reports.description: Monthly and periodic statistics on total banking-sector assets, resident and non-resident deposits, and gross bank credit by sector. NOTE: Grok's original claim of 'AED 5.5 trillion' does not match anything found in verification — 2025 reporting across multiple outlets clusters around AED 4-5tn (peak reported AED 4.97tn, June 2025). Treat any precise figure as unconfirmed until pulled from a CBUAE bulletin directly.

reports.title: Government Finance Statistics (GFS) — revenues, expenditures, assets and liabilities
reports.description: Official government finance statistics compiled according to the IMF Government Finance Statistics Manual 2014. Covers consolidated revenues, expenditures, assets and liabilities at the national level; quarterly and annual releases.

reports.title: Mubadala Investment Company assets under management and performance
reports.description: Annual reporting of assets under management, capital deployment, proceeds and long-term returns for Mubadala, one of Abu Dhabi's major sovereign investment vehicles. AUM reached AED 1.4 trillion (US$385 billion) in 2025 — VERIFIED exact match across multiple outlets (Arab News, The National, TradeArabia).

reports.title: Construction sector output and contract awards framing
reports.publisher: Federal Competitiveness and Statistics Centre (FCSC) — national accounts production series
reports.description: Construction sector output within FCSC national accounts production statistics (ISIC section F), plus contract-award framing. Construction is a major component of non-oil GDP, closely linked to real-estate, infrastructure and mega-project activity in both Dubai and Abu Dhabi. RESOLVED 2026-08-30: real primary source identified as FCSC national accounts (ISIC-classified), corroborated by Zawya quoting FCSC directly and by CBUAE Quarterly Economic Review sectoral tables sourced "FCSC and CBUAE calculations" — previously an unsourced placeholder (no url, no named publisher).

reports.title: Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) assets under management
reports.description: Abu Dhabi's traditional long-term sovereign wealth fund. AUM confirmed by UAE state media (Al Etihad) to have crossed US$1 trillion; other 2026 industry estimates (Bloomberg, The Middle East Insider) put ADIA specifically lower (~$870bn) within a combined Abu Dhabi sovereign-fund total of ~$1.7tn (ADIA+Mubadala+ADQ) — treat the ~$1tn figure as directionally right but not tightly precise. Invests primarily outside the UAE; core vehicle for intergenerational management of hydrocarbon surpluses.

reports.title: UAE exit from OPEC (effective 1 May 2026)
reports.description: One-off foundational event: the United Arab Emirates announced its departure from OPEC effective 1 May 2026, after 59 years of membership. The exit reduced OPEC's and OPEC+'s share of global crude production and capacity; the UAE retains independent production and export policy while remaining a major global supplier. VERIFIED independently by WAM (UAE state news agency), CFR, NPR, and Al Jazeera — this was the single most surprising claim across all 10 batches and it checked out completely.

reports.title: Federal Tax Authority — VAT and Corporate Tax revenue statistics
reports.description: UAE's tax administration — the direct analogue to Colombia's DIAN / Argentina's AFIP. Administers VAT (introduced 2018) and federal Corporate Tax (introduced 2023, 9% rate). VERIFIED: FTA 2025 Annual Report confirms VAT+excise collection reached AED ~46bn (up 15% y/y, ~$12.53bn). Missing entirely from all 10 original Grok batches despite being one of the most significant UAE fiscal developments of the past decade.

reports.title: Dubai International Airport (DXB) passenger traffic
reports.description: Official passenger traffic statistics for DXB. VERIFIED: 95.2 million passengers in 2025, a record year, and DXB became the world's busiest airport for international traffic (The National, Khaleej Times, Dubai Airports media office). Missing entirely despite ports, tourism and logistics all being covered — aviation is at least as central to Dubai's hub-economy story as Jebel Ali.

reports.title: IMF Article IV Consultation — United Arab Emirates
reports.description: Annual IMF Article IV consultation staff report and press release assessing UAE macroeconomic conditions, fiscal and monetary policy. VERIFIED real and current: 2025 Article IV Consultation staff report published December 2025; a follow-up staff visit concluded July 2026. Useful both as a real recurring node and as an independent cross-check source for UAE national statistics — completely absent from all 10 batches despite this pattern (an IMF programme/consultation node) already existing for other countries in this project.

dependencies.basis: WAM (UAE's own state news agency) and OPEC's continued MOMR publication both frame the exit as a change in OPEC/OPEC+ composition that the MOMR's ongoing market analysis must account for.
The UAE's departure is explicitly framed by multiple outlets (CFR, Al Jazeera) as an exit from both OPEC and the OPEC+ Declaration of Cooperation framework, not just OPEC membership alone.
The MOMR's supply-side analysis is structured around OPEC+ production-adjustment decisions made under the Declaration of Cooperation framework.
VAT and corporate tax collection are the primary tax-revenue input to the consolidated government finance statistics.
IMF Article IV consultations are built on the member country's own official national accounts data as the primary input to the Fund's macroeconomic assessment.
IMF Article IV inflation assessments are built on the member country's official CPI series.
Overnight visitor arrivals to Dubai are structurally downstream of air-passenger arrivals at DXB, the emirate's dominant entry point.
